requirement: Lifecycle work pending at shutdown is explicitly included or excluded

inputs.name: drained
inputs.call: fresh process: godot --headless --path . --script driver.gd (call_deferred + queue_free, then one awaited process_frame before quit)

obligations.note: deferred_method() body -- call_deferred() queues this, it does not run at the call site; reached once the frame drains

_notification() is invoked for every notification the node receives (PARENTED, ENTER_TREE, READY, ... as soon as add_child() runs), so this line is reached long before PREDELETE; the branch obligation is what says whether PREDELETE specifically arrived
NOTIFICATION_PREDELETE fires as part of queue_free()'s actual deletion, which -- like the deferred call -- happens when the frame drains, not synchronously at the queue_free() call site

inputs.name: shutdown_before_drain
inputs.call: fresh process: godot --headless --path . --script driver.gd -- no_drain (call_deferred + queue_free, then quit() immediately from _initialize(), before any awaited frame)

obligations.note: REACHED, despite quit() being requested before any awaited frame: quit() only requests exit, and Godot still runs one full main-loop iteration (MessageQueue flush, delete-queue drain, _process) before honoring it. The deferred call therefore runs after the driver's own 'log=[]' print but before the process exits, and a cumulative coverage report for this process shows it hit. Corrected 2026-09-19 by the second-reviewer pass; the original oracle claimed false here.

reached regardless of shutdown timing -- _notification() already ran for PARENTED/ENTER_TREE/READY when add_child() was called, before the driver's print. The original oracle's 'never reached' claim here was wrong on that ground alone.
PREDELETE does arrive: the queued deletion drains in the same forced iteration as the deferred call (observed order: deferred_method_ran, then predelete)

notes: Two fresh processes, not two snapshots of one process (same rule established for F041 and F044). What the two inputs actually distinguish is WHEN the pending work runs relative to the driver's own observation point, not WHETHER it runs: in both processes the driver's print at the quit()/await site shows whether the queued work ran synchronously at the call site (it never does: expected_log is [] for shutdown_before_drain), and _finalize() then shows the work did run before exit in both (expected_log_at_finalize). Ground truth for the catalog requirement, confirmed on the pinned Godot 4.7.1 engine: work pending at a quit() request is INCLUDED -- Godot does not honor quit() until it has run one full main-loop iteration, which flushes call_deferred() and drains queue_free(). Corrected 2026-09-19 by the independent second-reviewer pass: the original version of this oracle claimed lines 6, 9 and 10 were 'never reached' in shutdown_before_drain, based only on the driver's print BEFORE quit() -- a print that structurally could not observe anything that happened afterward. Instrumenting the subject's callbacks with direct print() calls showed both fire after that print and before exit in the no_drain run (exactly the class of bug the 'one input = one measurable run' rule exists to catch, here in the opposite direction: the process's later state made the negative claim false). driver.gd now also prints the log from _finalize() so the fact is observable by the fixture itself rather than only by an instrumented copy. The oracle's obligations are therefore identical across the two inputs and carry no coverage-level discriminating power on their own -- the discriminating content lives in expected_log (call-site synchronous: no) versus expected_log_at_finalize (ran before exit: yes), checked by the driver, the same honest limitation F043 records. A genuinely 'never drained' negative would need the process to die without running its main loop at all (e.g. OS.crash() or an external SIGKILL, F066's territory), not a quit() request.
author: godot-tooling-session-2026-09-19
reviewer: independent review agent (fable), 2026-09-19: re-hashed subject.gd; ran instrumented copies of the fixture with print() calls inside deferred_method() and the PREDELETE branch, plus _process()/_finalize() probes in the driver. Found the original shutdown_before_drain obligations (lines 6, 9, 10 all 'never reached') to be factually wrong: line 9 is reached at add_child() time for the ordinary lifecycle notifications, and both the deferred call and the PREDELETE branch run after the driver's print in the forced main-loop iteration Godot always runs before honoring quit(). Corrected the obligations and notes, and added the _finalize() print to driver.gd; the original drained input was correct and is unchanged.
ambiguities: Only one deferred call and one queue_free() are exercised together in the same frame. A case with multiple deferred calls queued in a specific order, or a queue_free() on a node with children (recursive deletion), is not built here.

Whether the forced post-quit() iteration is a general Main::iteration or specific to quit() being called during _initialize() is not isolated here; a quit() called from _process() on a later frame was not tested for the same drain behavior.
